# Further reference

## Csound and Blue

Blue produces Csound instruments and score events. If you are new to
Csound, learn the basic `instr`/`endin` structure and `i` and `f` score
statements before adapting examples in this book. Blue's generated CSD
preview is a useful bridge between the visual project and the Csound
code it runs. Use **Project → Generate CSD to Screen** while following
the [first project](first-project.qmd).

## Practical habits

- Keep related instrument code, local UDOs, and setup text together so
  the instrument can be copied into another project. See
  [Instrument types](instruments.qmd) and [UDOs](udos.qmd).
- Put reusable Score phrases in Project SoundObjects and create
  [Instances](instance.qmd) where linked editing is useful.
- Save the `.blue` project and its copied media folder together before
  moving them. Use [Project Properties](project-properties.qmd) to set the
  media folder.
- Preview generated CSD after changing score templates, processors,
  command blocks, or render options; this exposes the actual instrument
  IDs, note timing, and code order.

## Terms

**SoundObject** is a Score item that generates notes or other Csound
material. **BlueSynthBuilder** is an instrument with a widget interface.
**`pch`** is Csound's octave.pitch-class representation. **`p` field** is
one field of a Csound score event; `p1` is the instrument, `p2` start,
and `p3` duration. **UDO** means user-defined opcode. See the linked
chapters for their current controls.

## Compatibility notes

The Blue 2 manual's compatibility appendix describes a Java Blue
0.124.3 change: an automatable BlueSynthBuilder widget can produce a
control-rate signal even when a particular line is not automated. A
Csound expression using such a widget must accept that rate. This
remains useful when diagnosing older projects; verify the generated
CSD and current [automation](parameter-automation.qmd) behavior.

Older terms such as **blue Home** and the NetBeans-specific **`.blue`
directory** belong to the Java application. They should not be
used as current project-location instructions. Historical text and
links remain in the [Blue 2 source edition](https://github.com/kunstmusik/blue-manual/tree/7a92066a2aa8f0370026ba9527c158643c2935a1).
